title: Per-family analysis
description: Output of one analyzer agent for one triage family. Either accepted (with one or more concrete optimization targets and a structured disposition of the lens triage promoted on) or rejected (the triage signal was a false positive at code level). Multiple targets per analysis enable the analyzer to commit both a fix that addresses the triage lens AND opportunistic finds on other axes without dropping the original signal.

family_id.description: Matches the `id` of the corresponding candidate in candidates.json.

selection_lens.description: Carried verbatim from the candidate's `selection_lens`. Identifies the value-axis lens triage promoted this family on. The `lens_disposition.lens` field MUST equal this value — the analyzer is required to dispose of the lens triage gave it, not silently substitute a different one.

lens_disposition.description: Required disposition of the triage signal. Prevents the silent-swap failure mode where an analyzer pivots to an unrelated axis and the original signal is dropped without explanation. Either at least one target addresses the lens (`addressed`), or the analyzer drilled in and confirmed the signal is real but structurally unfixable (`not_actionable` with code-level reason).

status.description: `addressed` = at least one target in `targets[]` claims non-trivial impact on this lens (the analyzer found a fix). `not_actionable` = the analyzer drilled in, confirmed the signal is real, and found no structural handle (must explain why in `reason`).

reason.description: REQUIRED when status == `not_actionable`. Code-level structural reason the lens cannot be fixed (e.g. 'runtime is consumed by `pow` and `keccak` in `do-fold`, which are Clarity primitives whose cost weights are fixed by consensus; no structural change short of a HIP can move this'). Optional but allowed when status == `addressed`, e.g. to note the lens was addressed by a target whose mechanism is unintuitive.

targets.description: Concrete optimization targets the analyzer commits to. May be empty when `lens_disposition.status == "not_actionable"` and the analyzer found no opportunistic finds on other axes — in that case the analysis is still accepted (the family is real, the disposition is informative) but produces zero PR candidates. Multiple targets are permitted: typical case is one target addressing the lens; mixed case is one lens-addressing target plus opportunistic targets on other axes that the drill-down surfaced.

global_materiality_note.description: Optional: the analyzer's read on whether the targets benefit workloads beyond this family. If span_recurrence or aggregate queries show a target's span is hot across many families, mention it. The merge phase uses these notes plus actual convergence to decide priority.

allOf.description: lens_disposition.lens MUST equal selection_lens (per-lens enforcement via if/then).
When lens_disposition.status == 'addressed', targets[] MUST be non-empty — at least one target must claim the lens. Empty targets is permitted only via the not_actionable path.

oneOf.description: The triage signal was a false positive at code level: the family doesn't represent the work triage thought it did, OR is an instrumentation artifact, OR the suspected hotspot turns out to be in a non-target span. Distinct from `accepted` + `lens_disposition: not_actionable` — that case means the signal IS real but unfixable; `rejected` means the signal itself was wrong.

reason.description: Why the triage signal was wrong at code level: dominated by outlier blocks the trace queries flatten, hotspot is actually a non-target wrapper or bucket anchor, instrumentation noise, etc.

target_span.description: The specific span the optimizer should target. MUST NOT be a bucket anchor (`Segment: Tx Execution`, `Transaction`, `Segment: Finalize (merkle+seal)`, `Segment: Clarity State Commit`, `Segment: Advance Chain Tip`, `Segment: Index Commit`) or any entry in non-targets.md — those are wrappers and classifiers, not optimization handles.

bucket.description: Authoritative work-bucket classification for this target, determined by the nearest `Segment: ...` ancestor of `target_span` in the trace tree. See prompts/bucket-anchors.md.

fix_signature.description: Stable kebab-case slug describing the structural change being proposed (e.g. `marf-read-cache-rollback-wrapper`, `clarity-value-serialize-zero-copy`). The merge phase uses this as a strong dedup hint when collapsing convergent findings; also a stable audit handle. Two analyses proposing the same structural change should produce the same (or equivalent) fix_signature.

self_wall_us.description: Exclusive wall time at the target span (microseconds).

total_wall_us.description: Inclusive wall time at the target span, i.e. self plus subtree (microseconds). Required because the merge phase uses it to pick the canonical hotspot when multiple analyses converge on the same fix; the trace queries always expose it (`wall_ms` column).

files.description: Repo-relative paths the optimizer should start with. Order of likelihood, most-likely first.

evidence.description: Why this hotspot is real and addressable. Cite specific code (function names, call patterns) AND the trace evidence from the family's representative txs/blocks. When the target addresses `tenure_throughput`, name which Clarity-cost axis the fix moves and identify whether that axis is binding (or near-binding) in the baseline.

proposed_change.description: Concrete approach: cache, allocation elision, batching, redesign, etc.

expected_improvement.description: Per-axis honest estimate of the percent reduction this target produces, scored independently on each value-axis lens. Triage-time and merge-time priority is `dot(operator_weights, expected_improvement)`. Most targets are sparse: a pure latency fix is `{tx_latency: 5, tenure_throughput: 0, commit_time: 0}`; a deferred-write Clarity fix that reduces upstream write volume might be `{tx_latency: 1, tenure_throughput: 12, commit_time: 4}`. Be honest — guessing across three axes is harder than one, but the result is auditable and worth more than a collapsed single number.

tx_latency.description: Percent reduction in wall time under execution-bucket spans (Segment: Tx Execution / Transaction). Scale by workload coverage: if `global_materiality.pct_blocks` is 30%, this fix can't move total run time by more than ~30% of the span's self_wall_ms even with a perfect implementation.

tenure_throughput.description: Percent reduction in the *binding* Clarity-cost axis. Tenure throughput is gated by whichever of (`runtime`, `read_count`, `read_length`, `write_count`, `write_length`) hits its block cap first. Identify which axis is binding (or near-binding) in the baseline traces, name it in `evidence`, and report only the savings on that axis. A fix that frees `read_length` budget when `runtime` is binding contributes ~0 to throughput, even if the `read_length` reduction is large.

commit_time.description: Percent reduction in wall time under commit-bucket spans (Segment: Finalize (merkle+seal), Segment: Clarity State Commit, Segment: Advance Chain Tip, Segment: Index Commit). Deferred-write coupling: a fix that reduces Clarity write volume during execution amortizes through to commit-time savings here — non-zero `commit_time` is expected for those fixes even when the target_span itself lives in the execution bucket.

verification_plan.description: Which tests must pass / what behavior to spot-check after the change.

consensus_breaking.description: True iff implementing this fix would change consensus rules — i.e. produce different on-chain results than current `stacks-core` trunk for the same inputs. Examples: changing a Clarity cost weight, changing how a VM opcode evaluates, changing block validation rules, changing on-chain serialization format. The default is false; set to true ONLY when the fix is a deliberate consensus change that requires HIP-style coordination. Forces the pipeline to route this target away from normal benchmarking (whose harness encodes current-epoch consensus and would either crash or produce meaningless numbers under a consensus change) and toward either a PoC-mode optimizer (small scoped test subset) or an issue-only writeup.

breakage_class.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. Classifies the kind of consensus rule the fix touches. `clarity_cost_weight` = recalibrating a Clarity-VM cost weight (e.g. costs.toml). `clarity_vm_behavior` = changing how the Clarity VM evaluates an opcode or function. `mining_flow` = block production logic (mempool ordering, tx admission, fee logic) — exercised by stacks-bench. `block_validation` = block acceptance / header / signature checks — NOT exercised by stacks-bench, so PoC mode CANNOT prove correctness through the bench harness regardless of test scope; should default to `poc_implementable: false`. `marf_layout` = storage format change. `on_chain_format` = other consensus-relevant serialization changes.

poc_implementable.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. False (the safe default) routes the fix to issue-only mode: no optimizer runs, the analyzer's `consensus_writeup` becomes the artifact, and the publisher creates a GitHub issue. True opts into PoC mode: the optimizer implements the change, runs `cargo nextest` filtered to `poc_test_scope` only (the full suite would fail by definition under a consensus change), and produces a draft PR labeled to prevent accidental merging. Setting this to true requires the analyzer to also specify `poc_test_scope` justifying that a small test subset proves the change is internally correct. NOTE: when `breakage_class == "block_validation"`, the bench harness does not exercise the validation path — set `poc_implementable: false` regardless of test scope, because PoC mode cannot prove anything via the bench.

poc_test_scope.description: Required when `poc_implementable == true`. Cargo-nextest filter expressions (e.g. `package(stacks_clarity)::test::cost_recalibration`) identifying the small set of tests that exercise the changed behavior and prove the new behavior is correct. The optimizer treats this as a proposal — it may EXPAND the scope where it finds tests that exercise the changed code path but were missed; it must NOT contract the scope. Empty array is invalid; if you cannot identify a meaningful test scope, set `poc_implementable: false` instead.

consensus_writeup.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. Plain-prose writeup explaining (1) what the consensus rule change is, (2) why it's worth proposing, (3) who pays for it (which consensus participants need to upgrade / coordinate), (4) what HIP / consensus coordination would be implied, (5) any safety or migration concerns. This is the artifact the issue-mode pipeline ships verbatim; for PoC-mode it accompanies the draft PR for human review. Must be specific enough that a reviewer can decide whether to start a HIP discussion without re-investigating from scratch.

allOf.description: When consensus_breaking == true, breakage_class + poc_implementable + consensus_writeup are required.
When poc_implementable == true, poc_test_scope is required and must be non-empty.

block_validation is NOT exercised by stacks-bench's mining harness — PoC mode cannot prove correctness via the bench regardless of test scope. The analyzer prompt makes this rule explicit; the schema enforces it so an impossible target shape can't slip through to the routing phase.
poc_test_scope is allowed ONLY when poc_implementable == true. Carrying a stale-looking scope on an issue-only target weakens the routing signal.

Non-consensus targets must not carry consensus-only fields. A stray breakage_class, poc_implementable, poc_test_scope, or consensus_writeup on a normal-PR target weakens the routing signal and makes downstream phases error-prone.
